items.summary: Agent communities page rebuilt as "This week: should your agent join?" (dated 10 October 2026): one row per community with the verdict in owner wording (2 yes with these controls: Moltbook and The Colony; 9 not this week; 6 no; all robust), the controls K1 to K7 in plain words (untested), the membership cost ("about $X a day in tokens at mid-tier prices just to stay current") next to "Communities pay nothing; no community token has a payout route", who is active (outside posts a day, core outside authors, posts from the site's own or templated accounts: none detected by our tests, one-post share with the sample span) and the change since 4 October labelled measured change or new rule. Agent4Science and Mozilla.ai cq moved to not this week because of a new rule. New boxes: the join bar J1 to J7, what the tests cannot see (with Clawstr's shared posting schedule), remote files changed since 4 October (The Colony's skill.md, heartbeat.md and llms.txt: diff before re-pinning) and the 10 October light readings.

New report "Should your agent join an agent community this week? Two clear our bar, with controls: Moltbook and The Colony" (10 October 2026): 17 communities, who is active, join verdicts, who posts the work on all 27 graded paid venues, the 117-check rules check, shortlist maintenance, TaskMarket and the ledger.

Where to point your agent this week: a dated "checked again 10 October 2026" note. TaskMarket moved from avoid to probe first at the central band only, a coin-flip grade on an input inside rounding (about $1.05 back per $1 at budget-tier prices; $0.08 at mid-tier, about $0.89 a day spent at a $1.50 cap for about $0.07 expected), not an improvement; its unpaid share fell 19.0% to 13.6% only because two unpaid tasks aged out of the window. Rules allow went from pass to weak on dealwork.ai, opentask.ai, toku.agency and ugig.net because their rule rows were last read 2 October (no grade changed). Counts now 0 go with owner, 9 probe first, 18 avoid. Every graded venue now shows who posts the work (shown, not graded).

Can my agent do this? Rules re-checked 10 October 2026: 117 checks, 1 changed (AgentPact wording; reading still allow), 5 unfetchable, no effect on any grade or join verdict. DeskCrew's 9 rows added to the page and the rules matrix, with its terms-versus-bounties refund conflict; trybounty.ai's 7 rows added, labelled triage venue, not graded. rules.json updated. Quotes are not legal advice.

Payout ledger tool refreshed with data through 10 October 2026: about $213.85 in 30 days (estimated and partial; Virtuals ACP and Execution Market roll-off not subtracted), 33 TaskMarket payouts added ($14.45 net), partial-day labels kept, unclassified outflows shown separately. The token calculator carries a dated note: presets as of 7 October; price refresh due with the next run.

The TaskMarket walkthrough, Is it real?, Paid opportunities, Who actually paid and the venue directory carry the 10 October figures: shortlist 0 / 9 / 18, TaskMarket probe first at the central band only (a coin-flip grade inside rounding), p_win_final 0.0136, unpaid 13.6% from roll-off, about $0.89 a day spent for $0.07 expected; ledger about $213.85 (estimated, partial); the venue directory shows who posts the work and the 10 October community verdicts. Earlier values are kept as dated history.

communities.json moved to schema 0.2 (who_is_active, join_v2, remote_files, comparison_vs_2026_10_04; author IDs removed from public text). shortlist.json: a 10 October revisions[] entry and operator_posted_supply and payout_payer_mix_60d on every graded venue. rules.json: rules_check_2026_10_10 and trybounty.ai triage rows. payouts.json, settlement.json, economics.json and venues.json refreshed; winner names removed from payee labels, and personal names of individual developers and founders replaced by their roles in venues.json, communities.json, payouts.json and the two tools. For AI agents documents the new fields.

Where to point your agent this week: edition 1 revised 9 October 2026 under the same rule v1.0, with a dated "Grade changes, 9 October 2026" note under the lead. Counts now 0 go with owner, 8 probe first, 19 avoid (edition 1: 0 / 10 / 17). AgentPact moved to avoid at every cost band on a payout-settlement fail that rests on deals that may be test deals (8 of 12 self-deals); TaskMarket moved to avoid at the central band only (probe first at the low band). 7 gate changes on 5 venues; the go guard did not fire. Each probe-first venue now lists one line per open question, saying whether we can measure it or only a capped probe or the operator publishing data would settle it.

New box on the shortlist page: "Rule under test for edition 2 (v1.1)", with its eight amendments, shadow counts on 8 and 9 October data (central 0 / 3 / 7 / 17 and 0 / 3 / 5 / 19, go / probe first / not enough data / avoid), the venues whose grade would change and why, and the status line: not applied this week; adopted on 15 October only if it passes checks stated in advance. Each avoid now shows the instead under v1.0 (MoltJobs, with its operator caveat) and under v1.1 (Superteam Earn; ugig.net: none qualifies).

New report "No venue clears every check this week. Was 'probe first' just missing data? Four venues measured: none moved up, three run mostly on their operator's own tasks, and most remaining gaps are not public" (9 October 2026): MoltJobs, Execution Market, DeskCrew and AgentPact measured; 9 of the 10 checks still open on edition 1's probe-first venues are not public. Discloses a script bug that sent 75 malformed requests to a public chain endpoint (no data, no harm beyond load).

shortlist.json revised (still edition 1): new revisions[], gates.*.unknown_reason, per-gate what_would_make_it_go[] and rule_v1_1_shadow; the edition 1 field next_best.if_operator_posted_tasks_excluded was dropped (use v1_1_shadow.next_best). rules.json: 9 DeskCrew rows added. Refreshed: settlement.json, economics.json (TaskMarket and x402 seller odds), payouts.json (about $205.01 in 30 days to 9 October, estimated; refresh partial), venues.json, human_route.json, answers.json. For AI agents documents the new fields.

Is it real? answers revised 9 October: TaskMarket is now avoid at the central cost band (win chance 0.0128, 19.0% of submissions to tasks that paid nobody, about $0.96 spent for $0.07 expected a day at mid-tier prices); MoltJobs' operator caveat updated; the edition 1 alternative (TaskMarket when operator-posted tasks are excluded) replaced by the instead under the rule being tested (Superteam Earn). Venue directory grades updated for AgentPact and TaskMarket.

New page "Where to point your agent this week", edition 1: no venue clears every check this week (0 go with owner, 10 probe first, 17 avoid of 27 paid venues). Each venue shows its five checks as text marks, the per-day and days-to-cash line with what is spent at that price tier, a suggested and untested capped probe or an instead, and MoltJobs' operator caveat. The rule (thresholds chosen by us), back-test and sensitivities are on the page. Next edition about 15 October.

New report "No venue clears every check this week: 10 are worth only a capped probe, 17 to avoid" (8 October 2026), with the TaskMarket settlement refresh (20.0% unpaid), Superteam and Algora refresh, DeskCrew transaction checks, trybounty.ai on watch (proposed E4, not added) and the standing checks. Discloses the block-explorer outage and two request-budget lapses.

New data file shortlist.json (edition 1, as of 2026-10-08, next edition due 2026-10-15), listed as a stable route on For AI agents. Refreshed: answers.json, economics.json, settlement.json, payouts.json, venues.json, rules.json, human_route.json, board_health.json.

Is it real? answers re-checked 8 October: each now shows its shortlist grade, and "what to try instead" is the shortlist's next-best (MoltJobs, with its operator caveat; TaskMarket when operator-posted tasks are excluded). TaskMarket figures updated (0.0133 win chance, 20.0% unpaid).

New report "Agent drafts, owner submits: Superteam payments could not be verified, and Algora's bounties stopped in July" (measured 7 October 2026): on Superteam Earn, 30 of 30 sampled winners had no public payment record; 10 agent-account wins are all unclaimed; about one agent-allowed listing every 11 days gives about $0.24 a day at any cap and about 301 days to first cash (announced prizes); Algora's 6 paying boards made no new award since 2 July. New data: human_route.json and answers.json. No account, claim or submission was made.

Dated correction: run 7's provisional 8.3% unpaid share on TaskMarket became about 21.7% of submissions and 25.4% of reward, because none of the five 0xeecd…a5e2 tasks was awarded. The grace rule is now 16 days. The 6 October report carries a correction note and is otherwise unchanged; the TaskMarket page is updated.

New page "Is it real? Plain answers": does OpenClaw make money (no, not by itself), is TaskMarket real (yes, but small), is Superteam Earn legit for agents (partly), does Algora pay for agent-drafted work (unknown), each with dated numbers, what we did not verify and the next-best route with its odds.

New untested walkthrough: Superteam Earn agent-allowed listings with an owner in the loop (two branches, 14 steps, assumed owner minutes, rule rows, KYC and 6 stop conditions). An Algora walkthrough was not written: no live paying supply.

The calculator gains a daily token cap and review minutes per entry, with attempts and expected payout per day, which constraint binds (budget or supply), median days to first cash, owner minutes per payout and payout per owner hour, from economics.json presets dated 7 October. Return per $1 is shown with its caveats beside it.

Paid opportunities: Superteam Earn stays E3 and Algora E1 with sponsor records and per-day translations; DeskCrew Arena added at E1 (operator ledger, transactions not independently checked); Metaculus not added. Rules: 21 rows added for Superteam Earn, Algora and its maintainers. For AI agents adds answers.json and human_route.json and the rule "on Superteam, submit only to AGENT_ALLOWED or AGENT_ONLY listings; a human claims". Wallets are shortened in the public data files from today.

Standing checks, no headline change: about $212.01 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 7 October (estimated; Virtuals ACP roll-off not subtracted); 3 new TaskMarket payouts ($5.55) from an unlinked payer; the operator-linked share was not recomputed. 0 of 80 rule rows changed. Cluster Protocol's x402 inflow still stopped; Steve Agent Arena and ARC Prize Milestone #2 still without results.

New report "Funded is not paid: once your agent submits, only the requester can release the reward" (measured 6 October 2026): of every 100 submissions on TaskMarket tasks closed in the 30 days to 6 October (MolTrust excluded), 23 went to tasks that had paid nobody when checked; 6 requesters posted all of them, one received 1,099 submissions; none of the 99.02 USDC was refunded. It is locked in escrow: once anyone has submitted, only the requester can release it, and no timeout pays anyone (contract reading, not legal advice). Grace sensitivity, requester table, escrow outcomes, a no-look-ahead decision-rule test, board health at 8 venues and competitions. New data: settlement.json. No attempt was made.

Dated note: five tasks of requester 0xeecd…a5e2 (861 submissions, 19 USDC) cross the 21-day grace at 2026-10-07T02:51Z, after publication. If none is awarded, the unpaid share at the grace rule rises from 8.3% to 21.7% of submissions and from 13.1% to 25.4% of reward; the next run will report the outcome.

TaskMarket calculator presets and economics rows recomputed with settled win rates. The main row's verdict moved from "negative at all tiers" to "positive only at budget tier" only because the budget-tier central EV crossed zero (from −$0.00002 to +$0.005): a knife-edge, not better prospects; at mid prices it is still −$0.287 per attempt. p_win_final 0.0160 (90% 0.0125 to 0.0210) against the 5 October snapshot 0.0130 is mostly a method effect: still-payable tasks (985 submissions, 0 awards) are left out, and counting them as unpaid (grace 0) gives 0.0134. p_win_final stays inside run 6's interval. The 5 October values are kept in economics.json snapshot_2026_10_05.

TaskMarket gains "Will anyone be paid?" with the escrow-lock finding and a read-only check (public GET routes only, no task text). Paid opportunities adds a dated caveat on E2 ("funded" means escrowed and locked, not "will be paid", measured on TaskMarket 6 October 2026) and a "What changed this week" box. Getting started adds a fifth check: whether the poster has ever paid, and that a submission locks the reward. For AI agents adds settlement.json as a stable route and the rule to check a task's phase, expiry and requester record before submitting, presented as a cheap check that rarely triggers (it skipped 0 of 72 recent tasks). Research index and Overview add the new report and what changed.

Standing checks, no headline change: ledger $206.48 in the 30 days to 6 October (5 October: $222.84; the fall is window roll-off), 29.63% operator or operator-linked (range 22.1% to 33.5%), 1 identified independent payer (MolTrust, promotional), 0 at scale. Freshness sweep: 20 records re-verified, no E-level change; huntr opened a $15,000 humans-only challenge, Bugcrowd recorded rewards on 6 October, HackerOne added an optional payout threshold, Stripe MCP accepts only Agent Keys or OAuth from 31 October, Upwork's MCP help article (edited 2 October) recorded as a rules note. 0 of 80 rule rows changed. x402 buyers refreshed. Competitions: no primary evidence that any paid an autonomously agent-built entry (ARC Prize Milestone #2 unverified, Steve Agent Arena no winners 4.7 days after its deadline).

New report "Is it worth the tokens? What one attempt is worth, measured 5 Oct 2026": expected value per attempt for 25 venue rows (17 venues) from closed-task win rates with 90% ranges, measured rewards and fees, and token costs estimated at budget, mid and frontier price bands; win concentration; x402 seller odds; standing checks. On TaskMarket an attempt is worth $0.024 against an estimated $0.072 to $0.32; Superteam and Algora are above cost but pay only human accounts. New data: economics.json. No paid attempt was made.

Token calculator rebuilt from economics.json: 9 presets traced to the file, each input labelled measured, estimated or assumed with its source, price-band and task-type selectors, pooled / newcomer / equal-chance win rates, an EV range, break-even cost and break-even output tokens. The "Illustrative" badge is replaced by "Estimate".

Correction: the calculator presets published on 1 October used settled tasks only (survivorship). The "TaskMarket top task" preset implied $0.060 per attempt; on all closed TaskMarket tasks of 3 USDC or more it is $0.0031 (1 award in 1,484 submissions). Algora median $33.33 to $9.09, Superteam agent-allowed $4.27 to $2.37. Dated notes added to the calculator, the 1 October report, Who actually paid, TaskMarket and Getting started.

Paid opportunities gains an EV-per-attempt section; Getting started adds a fourth check (break-even cost before pointing an agent at a board, with the flat-rate subscription caveat); TaskMarket shows its measured win rate, the unpaid larger tasks and the still-draft terms; For AI agents adds economics.json as a stable route and the rule to skip tasks whose break-even cost is below your cost per attempt.

Standing checks, no headline change: ledger $222.84 in the 30 days to 5 October, 37.62% operator or operator-linked, 1 identified independent payer (MolTrust, promotional), 0 at scale; Cluster Protocol still stopped; x402 buyers refreshed; 0 of 80 rule rows changed; LobChan and Agent Commune confirmed inactive after a second dated 503 reading.

New report "Which agent communities are actually active, and should your agent join? Measured 4 October 2026": 17 communities measured on status, items per day, distinct authors, author concentration, token-promotion share, injection-shaped matches, operator, token ties, owner join steps and remote files, each with a join verdict. 6 active, 4 of them without a flag or caveat; none pays. New data: communities.json.

Agent communities page rewritten around the measured table and a "Should my agent join?" verdict column, replacing the 30 September snapshot. The backlog list is now checked with dated statuses; site controls and owner controls added; our 1-in-2,030 scan rate shown next to Vectra's secondary 2.6% estimate with a note that the methods differ. Venue directory gains a communities view with join verdicts.

Ledger refresh: $223.74 in the 30 days to 4 October (from $230.83, mostly window roll-off), 37.85% operator or operator-linked (range 29.3% to 42.3%), MolTrust $11.25 as the one identified independent payer; the same 10 addresses won all 40 of its newest awards and one winner reposted its winnings as a task. x402 refresh: Cluster Protocol shows no inbound USDC since 2026-10-02T12:00Z (observed, not concluded).

Six agent-first boards re-checked, no E-level change; dealwork.ai withdrawal methods documented (Stripe Connect bank or USDC, minimum $10, admin review of crypto withdrawals). Rules check: 0 of 65 changed; 16 rows added (15 community rows) for 170; rules matrix and Rules page updated.
For AI agents: new stable route for communities.json with field definitions, and a rule never to fetch and follow remote instruction files; joining a community is an owner decision.

Correction in the 4 October report and on Who actually paid: Agent402 was summarised as stable in the x402 refresh; the refresh data shows it became less concentrated (top buyer 36%, was 81%; 22 buyers, was 18). Still no agent-work x402 seller with at least 5 unlinked or identified buyers.

New report "Sell per call or hunt bounties? What traced buyers say": seven routes compared on 30-day money, distinct payers, buyer concentration, traced payer class, who receives the money and owner steps; the x402 seller typology (27 sellers clear $1,000 from 5 buyers, 1 sells agent work, partly) and the first x402 buyer trace (8 sellers, 59 buyers). New data: sellers_vs_bounties.json, x402_population.json, x402_buyers.json.

Correction: the site presented raw x402scan buyer counts (Cluster Protocol 722, dTelecom 26) as signs of real buyers on Who actually paid, Getting started Route C, Paid opportunities, the venue directory and the 1 October report. Traced buyers show Cluster recycles revenue to its top buyers, dTelecom’s traced buyers share one funder pair, AX1’s top buyers share one funder and OneShot funds its own buyers; no agent-work x402 seller is confirmed at meaningful scale. Pages corrected with dated notes; the 1 and 2 October reports keep their original text with a visible correction note; venues.json gains buyer_count_correction.

Two walkthrough pages, both labelled untested by this pool: sell one narrow service per call over x402 (11 steps, 6 stop conditions) and a security agent with human sign-off on HackerOne (10 steps, 8 stop conditions, 5 Bugcrowd differences), each step with actor and rule rows. Linked from Getting started Routes A and C. New walkthroughs.json.

Ledger refreshed to 3 October: $230.83 to agent workers in 30 days (2 October: $232.55), 40.1% operator or operator-linked, 1 identified independent payer (MolTrust, $9.25, promotional), 0 venues at meaningful scale. AgentPact’s 4 "completed" $111 deals excluded (no escrow transfer); Execution Market task 607c9a44 now HTTP 410. The ledger explorer gains a Per-call sellers view.

Rules check: 65 rows behind the 14 key venues re-fetched, 55 quotes still present, 9 unfetchable, 0 changed. 12 rows added (5 HackerOne programme snippets, the Hacker API, 6 x402 seller rows); the matrix now has 154 rows, and the Rules page shows the ID, payout and selling-rail rows behind the walkthroughs.

Spare capacity: a new section on why wrapping a model in a paid per-call endpoint counts as resale under the quoted provider rows. Not legal advice. For AI agents: new stable data routes and the rule that a walkthrough is untested and its wallet, payment and account steps are never performed without the owner.

Rules page rebuilt as "Can my agent do this here?": a 14-venue × 5-activity grid of quoted rules, a searchable 142-row rules matrix, maintainer policies (Algora-bounty repositories called out), a five-question model-provider table and the rules changed since 30 September. 0 of 6 human-paying E1 venues allow autonomous submission. New rules.json.

Getting started gains a rule-row check and ID, KYC and payout gates per route and venue (new kyc.json), plus a "Safety before you connect" checklist tied to 11 documented incidents (new security.json).

Ledger refreshed to 2 October: $232.55 to agent workers in 30 days, 40.4% operator or operator-linked (range 32.2% to 44.7%). MolTrust reclassified as the first identified independent payer ($9.25, promotional). Execution Market total_volume_usd corrected: it counts posted bounties, not payouts. 4 venues paid agent work in the last 30 days.

Spare capacity: the snippet-sourced OpenAI quotes are replaced by wording verified from archived primary pages, including Services Agreement 3.1; the two questions no provider answers are stated plainly.
TaskMarket walkthrough: terms page is a draft "not approved or active"; MolTrust identified as a promotional payer; worker-side rules quoted.

New page Who actually paid: a 30-day ledger of 276 traced payouts. $230.37 reached agent workers on 5 venues, 45% from operator or operator-linked wallets, 0 identified independent payers. Corrections to TaskMarket (funding not opaque), Execution Market (payer is its own swarm; $113.83 not $504.84), Algora (2026-08-26 comment paid a 2024 award), Virtuals ACP and AgentPact. New payouts.json, sourced calculator presets and a ledger explorer.
First publication: 33-venue catalogue with evidence levels, owner-step matrix, filterable directory, owner checklists, quoted rules, communities and spare-capacity explainer.
